THE CONTROL THAT MAKES THOSE ZEROS MEAN SOMETHING: '  CONTROL, the @<hex> detector alive: 2 of 61 proposals carry a bare @<hex> -- a NON-ZERO, so the three zeros above are ABSENCES measured by a live instrument, not dead reads', and on 2026-09-04 the positive control resolves to the literal string '@351f309e' inside proposal 9's evidence_cited; a NEGATIVE control ('NFRA_OUTSET-W', which must not appear) returns 0 of 10; the patterns ran over 3,040 characters across that day's 10 strings. mutant.description: THERE IS NO CODE MUTANT ON THIS CELL AND THAT IS NOT AN OMISSION: this order grants no repo surface, so nothing was built that a mutant could break. The equivalent control on an INSPECTION is the one that decides whether a zero means anything -- a POSITIVE control run on the same corpus and through the same detector family as the zeros, plus a NEGATIVE control for a token that must not appear. Without it, '0 of 61 cite a tool row' and 'my regex is dead' are the same bytes.
mutant.expected: the @<hex> detector must return a NON-ZERO on the same 61 evidence_cited strings that returned zero for path@vintage, comp-* and .json -- and the negative token must return zero
mutant.observed: FIRED. 2 of 61 proposals match @<hex>, and on 2026-09-04 the match resolves to the literal '@351f309e' inside proposal 9's evidence_cited. The negative control 'NFRA_OUTSET-W' returned 0 of 10 on that day. So the three zeros are ABSENCES measured by a live instrument. Also deliberate: comp-find CONTENT mode was NOT used anywhere in this cell -- the corpus is a fetched JSON document parsed structurally, not the repo, so neither of that tool's measured false-zero modes (rc=124 with no output; rc=0 with a confident denominator and no budget line) is in this path at all.

determinism.method: the census was run on ONE day first and then on SEVEN, because a single day's reading is a one-day pattern and a one-day pattern is tested by dates outside it. The producer comparison was run on two planes (the served S3 artifact and HEAD) and on CONTENT tokens rather than on filename or size alone.
